A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FedTreeLoRA and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite pagination and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original GLUE accuracy and FLAN ROUGE-1 experiments, motivational studies, ablations, and additional BLOOM results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds warm-up sensitivity and client-joining experiments in Appendices C.5–C.6.

M1.justification: Appendix C.6 adds an incremental-client procedure: a joining client warms up locally, uses its LoRA B matrices to identify the closest existing branch, and then participates in layer-wise aggregation. The original method in Section 5 and Algorithm 1 remains unchanged.

E1.justification: The GLUE and FLAN datasets and tasks are retained. Appendix C.6 adds a distinct MNLI scenario involving clients joining during training, extending evaluation beyond fixed client populations.

E2.justification: The new client-joining comparison evaluates the arriving client against local-only training in Table 16. Local training already appeared in motivational studies, but this comparator participation is new. The six named federated baselines remain unchanged in the retained benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: The added experiments compare five versus ten warm-up epochs and client arrival at communication round 10 versus 20. The joining study samples a different arriving client for each setting and includes no-joining and local-only controls. Existing benchmark protocols are retained; these additions do not establish a changed default training budget.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.5 tests sensitivity to warm-up duration, while C.6 examines whether client insertion disrupts existing clients and benefits newcomers. These are limited additions to the substantial sensitivity and ablation analyses already present in v1.

E5.justification: The existing three-independent-run statements and uncertainty entries are retained. New Tables 15–16 provide point estimates without introducing additional run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. New Table 15 reports averages of 87.80 and 87.81 for five and ten warm-up epochs; the five-epoch scores repeat Table 13's task-heterogeneity values. New Table 16 reports newcomer scores of 84.50 versus 82.00 for local-only training at round 10, and 86.50 versus 79.00 at round 20, with small declines for existing clients.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Theorem 5.1, Assumptions A.1–A.3, and complete convergence proof in Appendix A are unchanged. The new topology discussion adds empirical reasoning rather than a formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about dual heterogeneity, tree-structured layer-wise aggregation, and improved NLU/NLG performance with negligible parameter overhead.

C2.justification: Appendix C.5 newly interprets warm-up stability as evidence that useful client relationships emerge early, supporting a fixed topology. C.6 explicitly identifies the primary fixed-population scope and interprets the joining results as evidence of topology reuse for incremental personalization.

D1.justification: New Appendix J supplies an implementation repository address and describes preprocessing, training, evaluation, setup instructions, and configurable ablations. v1 already disclosed warm-up budgets, hardware, and pseudocode. The PDFs establish the added access information; repository completeness remains unverified.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds several federated-learning references, and Appendix I adds a substantive distinction from resource-oriented layer allocation in Fed-HELLO. The earlier TreeLoRA distinction is retained. Publication updates for LoRA-FAIR, FedALT, and FedLEASE refer to the same previously cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and heading additions, expands the appendix contents, inserts a reproducibility section, and adds acknowledgments and an impact statement. Publication text changes to conference proceedings information. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds two compact tables for warm-up and client-joining results. Existing appendix Tables 15–19 become Tables 17–21, with accompanying figure/table relocation and page reflow. All eight existing figures are retained without substantive visual changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides useful additional evidence about warm-up sensitivity and client insertion, clarifies positioning against layer-aware resource allocation, and supplies explicit code-access information. These improve practical assessability while preserving the original evidence. The gains are limited because the new tables omit uncertainty and leave some settings underdescribed; they do not substantially strengthen the unchanged central results or theory.
